question.leadin: Name these Latin American nations that were the site of twentieth-century violence.
question.text: A CIA-backed 1973 coup in this nation led to the suicide of president Salvador Allende in Santiago's La Moneda Palace.
question.clue: As a colony, this country was Spain's leading supplier of saltpeter.

swap.leadin: He met with Jose de San Martin at the Guayaquil Conference.
swap.text: Name this early 19th-century South American leader nicknamed "The Liberator."
swap.clue: This man led forces meant to dismantle an administrative unit known as Real Audencia, which culminated in his victory at the 1822 battle of Pichincha.

question.text: Founded by Francisco Pizarro and situated on the Pacific Ocean, this city is the capital and largest city of Peru..
question.clue: This city, which has its seaport at Callao, draws its water from the Rimac, Lurin, and Chillon Rivers.

swap.leadin: The Mariel boatlift was a sharp increase in immigration from this country to the United States, which has utilized the "wet feet, dry feet" policy since 1995.
swap.text: Name this Caribbean nation, to which Elian Gonzalez was repatriated in 2000.
swap.clue: The only U.S. territory on this island is a naval base at Guantanamo ("GWAHN-TAHN-uh-mo") Bay.

question.leadin: This man was imprisoned for a year on the Isle of Youth.
question.text: Name this revolutionary, who led the 26th of July Movement to overthrow Fulgencio (fool-JEN-see-oh) Batista.
question.clue: Che Guevara joined this man's 26th of July Movement.

swap.leadin: This man was pursued by General "Blackjack" Pershing following a 1916 raid on Columbus, New Mexico.
swap.text: Name this figure from the Mexican Revolution known for his incursions into the U.S.
swap.clue: This man's capture of Ojinaga was delayed because the cameramen filming the battle had to move into position first.

question.text: This island was the site of Tacky's revolt in 1760. In 1831, this island was also the site of a slave rebellion led by Samuel Sharpe, the Baptist War, also known as the Christmas uprising.
question.clue: Simon Bolivar advocated for a united Latin America in a letter from this island, where he was exiled to in 1815.

swap.leadin: Name some incidents during the Banana Wars.
swap.text: This country saw many American interventions related to the United Fruit Company and the Cuyamel Fruit Company, whose influence over leaders of this country like Manuel Bonilla led O. Henry to coin the term "banana republic."
swap.clue: Patricia Rodas left this country for asylum in Mexico during events that led to the overthrow of Manuel Zelaya and the installation of Roberto Micheletti in a 2009 coup.

question.leadin: This country's second president Floriano Peixoto (pay-SHOH-too), suppressed the Revolta da Armada and overthrew an emperor who later fled to Portugal.
question.text: Name this country, which became a republic in 1889 after its first president, Deodoro da Fonseca, ousted an emperor.
question.clue: The Integralists and a public works advocate of Gypsy descent named Juscelino Kubitschek hailed from this country, whose leaders once lived in Catete Palace.

swap.leadin: This man was promoted to be a member of the Sagunto Dragoons following the Battle of Albuera in Spain.
swap.text: Identify this general, who replaced Manuel Belgrano following the Battle of Tucuman. He'd win the Battle of Maipu and liberate Santiago, Chile.
swap.clue: This leader defeated Manuel Osorio alongside Bernardo O'Higgins at Maipu after winning at Chacabuco.

question.text: The official song of the Marines, the "Marines' Hymn," begins "From the halls of Montezuma," which refers to the Marines' storming of this castle guarding Mexico City. The six "Boy Heroes" died trying to defend this location.
question.clue: It's been the site of the National History Museum since 1939, after the official residence of its country's leader was moved to Los Pinos.

swap.text: This 20th-century dictator of Haiti, nicknamed "Papa Doc," employed the brutal Tonton Macoutes secret police.
swap.clue: This former administrator of a yaws eradication campaign was a follower of Lorimer Denis and thus joined the mystic Groupe des Griots.

question.leadin: Richard Nixon supposedly told Richard Helms to "make the economy scream" in response to the election of this leader.
question.text: Name this leader. Orlando Letelier, this leader's ambassador to the U.S., tried to negotiate the nationalization of his country's copper mines.
question.clue: U.S. officials supported this leader's opponent, Jorge Alessandri, in the presidential election of 1970.

swap.text: Many refugees settled in British Honduras during a late 19th-century Mayan revolt named for this concept, which also names a system in colonial Spanish America that officially categorized mestizo and mulatto individuals.
swap.answerHtml: caste [or casta; accept casta system or Caste War of Yucatán or ba'atabil kichkelem Yúum]
swap.clue: Opposition to this system is symbolized by the red stripe on the flag of the Army of the Three Guarantees.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Latin American wars.
question.text: This 1836-1839 war was sparked when Peru and Bolivia attempted to merge into the single namesake country. It turned when Chile joined the effort after a series of comical misunderstandings and abortive coups turned reviled general Diego Portales into a national martyr.
question.answerHtml: War of the Confederation [accept: War of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation; Guerra contra la Confederación Perú-Boliviana]
question.clue: Diego Portales, the powerful defense minister who started this war, was assassinated in its second year, greatly increasing public support for this conflict on the winning side.

swap.leadin: This region was not colonized by the British or Americans due to the Clayton-Bulwer Treaty.
swap.text: Name this region of Central America bordering the Caribbean Sea, that includes the city of Bluefields. Although this region's name refers to a group of natives, it is often spelled after a certain insect.
swap.clue: The "Cleopatra Affair" involved the landing of a British force at Bluefields, the capital of this region, in violation of the Clayton-Bulwer treaty.

question.leadin: This man was deposed with CIA help after trying to expropriate lands held by the United Fruit Company.
question.text: Identify this man who was part of an officer revolt against Jorge Ubico and succeeded Juan Jose Arevalo as president of his nation.
question.clue: This leader who passed Decree 900, an agrarian reform law that redistributed unused lands from large plantations to peasants in exchange for government bonds.

swap.text: Cuba is sometimes credited for organizing opposition to Jose Napoleon Duarte in this country, where a leftist party was legitimized after the Chapultepec Peace Accords of 1992.
swap.clue: The killing of Rutilio Grande in this country prompted liberation theologian, Archbishop Oscar Romero, to refuse to attend state occasions.

question.leadin: This leader came to prominence as a historian, writing such books as Capitalism and Slavery before entering politics to lead the People's National Movement.
question.text: Name this first post-independence Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago.
question.clue: Prior to becoming the leader of the People's National Movement, or PNM, this man wrote a 1944 history arguing that the British empire abolished the slave trade for economic reasons and not for moral ones.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a ruler whose control of the Dominican Republic was known as the "Platano Curtain."
swap.text: This man was elected president in 1930 when a rebellion toppled Horacio Vasquez's government. He later banned all other political parties, renamed Santo Domingo, the province of San Cristobal, and the country's highest mountain after himself. He also oppressed Haitians in his country.
swap.clue: He also ordered the killings of the Mirabal Sisters, and the failure of general Pupo Roman to act following this man's death allowed Johnny Abbes Garcia to catch and punish most of his assassins.
